lines.japanese: やっぱりね。五分なんてあっという間でしたよ。
lines.english: Just as I thought. Five minutes passed in the blink of an eye.

lines.japanese: プラットホームとひと続きのコンコース。自動改札の向こうに、週末の夜を楽しんだお客さんをたらふく呑みこんで、アルミ色の下り電車が発車時刻を待っています。
lines.english: The concourse opened directly onto the platform. Beyond the automatic gates, an aluminum-colored outbound train sat waiting to depart, its belly packed with passengers returning from their weekend revels.

lines.japanese: 「お待たせしましたー」
lines.english: “Sorry to keep you waiting.”

lines.japanese: 意外なことに日和子さんは、俺が切符を買うまで待っていてくれました。
lines.english: To my surprise, Hiyoko had waited while I bought my ticket.

lines.japanese: 券売機の列から戻ってくると、太い角柱のそばに寄りかからず立っていた彼女は一回うなずきました。
lines.english: When I returned from the ticket-machine line, Hiyoko stood perfectly upright beside a thick square pillar. She gave a single nod.

lines.japanese: 「はい。それじゃ──」
lines.english: “All right, then—”

lines.japanese: ぺこり。
lines.english: A little bow.

lines.japanese: 「──失礼します。お休みなさい」
lines.english: “—Excuse me, then. Good night.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、ども、オヤスミっすー」
lines.english: “Ah, sure. Night.”

lines.japanese: と俺たちは「さよなら」も「また今度」もなく、いったん解散しかけたのですが。
lines.english: And so, without either 'goodbye' or 'see you again,' we very nearly went our separate ways.

lines.japanese: 「あー、えー……ちょっとー……」
lines.english: “Ah, um... Hold on...”

lines.japanese: どうにも引っかかるところがあって、やっぱり俺は日和子さんを呼びとめました。
lines.english: Something continued to nag at me, so in the end I called Hiyoko back.
“—Yes?”

lines.japanese: 「えーっと、あの、最後にちょっといいすか」
lines.english: “Um, could I ask you one last thing?”

lines.japanese: 「はあ」
lines.english: “What is it?”

lines.japanese: 俺はまだ穴の空いていない小さな紙片で、ぱたぱた顔を扇いだりしていました。
lines.english: I fanned my face with the little paper ticket that had yet to be punched.

lines.japanese: こんな風に改札の前で言葉を濁していると、なんだか、わずかな逢瀬の名残を惜しむ遠距離恋愛カップルみたいですよね。
lines.english: Standing here before the gates and fumbling for words, we must have looked like a long-distance couple reluctant to end a precious little rendezvous.

lines.japanese: でもそんな風に思われたら困りますので（いや日和子さんがね）、俺はさっさと切りだしました。
lines.english: That would have been terribly awkward if anyone got the wrong idea—for Hiyoko, I mean—so I came straight to the point.

lines.japanese: 「や、実はですね。俺、メンフリだけじゃなくて、いろんなバイト掛け持ちでやってんですけど──」
lines.english: “The truth is, Men's Freeze isn't my only job. I juggle a whole bunch of part-time work—”

lines.japanese: 「──ていうか、そもそもあれは副業中の副業でたまにやらせてもらってる程度なんです」
lines.english: “—Actually, that one barely even counts. They only give me work now and then.”

lines.japanese: 日和子さんは例によって頷いたり相槌を打ったりはせず、しかし視点だけはしっかり相手の目に置くというお馴染みの態度で俺の話を聞いていました。
lines.english: As usual, Hiyoko listened without nodding or offering little sounds of encouragement, yet kept her gaze fixed firmly on my eyes.

lines.japanese: 「でー、俺さっきマスターから、アレキサンダーの臨時ヘルプ頼まれたんすよ」
lines.english: “Anyway, the boss asked me earlier to help out at Alexander for a while.”

lines.japanese: 「はい」
lines.english: “I see.”
“What?!”

lines.japanese: ええ、まあ、驚きますよね。
lines.english: Yeah, well, of course she'd be surprised.

lines.japanese: 「や、まだ返事はしてなくて、どーしようか考え中なんですけど」
lines.english: “I haven’t answered him yet. I’m still deciding what to do.”

lines.japanese: 「ぶっちゃけどーすかね。俺、断った方がいいすかね」
lines.english: “Honestly, what do you think? Should I turn him down?”

lines.japanese: 「はあ？」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: はあ。いろんな『はあ』を使いこなすひとだなあ。はあ。
lines.english: Huh. She could play more variations on a single huh than anyone I'd ever met. Huh.

lines.japanese: 「なんで……え、千歳さんの好きにされたらいいんじゃないですか」
lines.english: Why would... Um, shouldn't you just do whatever you want?

lines.japanese: 日和子さんはちらりと視線を外しながら、驚き少々を混ぜた無関心な調子で言いました。
lines.english: Hiyoko glanced away and answered with studied indifference, though a touch of surprise colored her voice.

lines.japanese: 「いやあ、だからなんてーか、ぶっちゃけなんですけど……ほら俺、あんまり日和子さんに良く思われてないっぽいじゃないですか」
lines.english: Well, I mean, to be totally honest... you know, it kinda feels like you don't think very highly of me.

lines.japanese: 「はい」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese: 「はい」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese: うわあ、生返事でも言いなおさないパターンあるんだあ。しょぼーん。
lines.english: Wow, so sometimes she doesn't take back the automatic answer. I deflated.

lines.japanese: 「でも、そんなの千歳さんには関係ないじゃないですか。それとも、千歳さんは仕事を決めるのに、いちいち他人の顔色を窺うんですか」
lines.english: “But that has nothing to do with you. Or do you let other people’s reactions decide every job you take?”

lines.japanese: 「そりゃそうでしょ。いつだって、若者がバイトを辞める理由の第一位は人間関係っすよ。普通、普通」
lines.english: Well, of course. Problems with coworkers are always the number-one reason young people quit part-time jobs. Totally normal. Totally.

lines.japanese: 口を開いたものの言葉は出てこない日和子さん。心当たりでもあったのでしょうか。
lines.english: Hiyoko opened her mouth, but no words emerged. Had that struck a nerve?

lines.japanese: 普通、普通。
lines.english: Normal. Totally normal.

lines.japanese: 「……なんにしても、私から申しあげることはありません。ご自分で決めてください」
lines.english: ...In any case, I have nothing to say about it. Decide for yourself.

lines.japanese: 「え、いんすか？　あらまあ。でしたら、ひとこと賛成だと言ってください」
lines.english: “Really? Well, then. In that case, just say you approve.”

lines.japanese: 「やですよ」
lines.english: “I don't want to.”

lines.japanese: 「なんで！　反対じゃないなら賛成してくださいよ！」
lines.english: “Why? If you're not against it, then be for it!”

lines.japanese: 「いやです。べつに賛成というほどではありませんので」
lines.english: “No. I would not go so far as to say that I approve.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ、やっぱ反対なんすか。あーそーすか、俺が働くのに反対なんすか」
lines.english: “So you do object after all. Ah, I see. You object to me working there.”

lines.japanese: 「違います。中立です。私には関係がないと言ってるんです」
lines.english: “That is not what I said. I am neutral. I said it has nothing to do with me.”

lines.japanese: 「え、え、じゃあですよ？　中立とかナシにして、反対か賛成か、どっちかって言うとどっちなんですか」
lines.english: W-wait, then answer me this. No neutral. If you had to pick, are you for it or against it?

lines.japanese: 「ど、どっちかって言うと？」
lines.english: “I-if I had to choose?”

lines.japanese: 「どっちかって言うと」
lines.english: “If you had to choose.”

lines.japanese: 「ど、どっちかって言うと……」
lines.english: “If... if I had to choose...”

lines.japanese: 「どっちかって言うとっ！？」
lines.english: “If you had to choose?!”
“...I... object?”

lines.japanese: いや、そんなしおらしく遠慮がちに言われても──言わせたの俺ですけど。
lines.english: No, saying it all meek and hesitant like that isn't—okay, I'm the one who made her say it.

lines.japanese: 「デスヨネーッ！」
lines.english: “KNEW IT!”

lines.japanese: ていうか、なんでわざわざ言わせたんですかね俺は。ひょっとして、もう一方の答えでもほのかに期待してたのかしら。あらら、鷲介君ったらおめでたい子だわ。
lines.english: Why had I gone to such lengths to make her say it, anyway? Could I possibly have harbored some faint hope of the other answer? Well, aren't you a sweet little fool, Shusuke.

lines.japanese: 「ええ、じゃあ、その貴重なご意見は参考にさせていただきます。ま、日和子さんがなんて言おうと、最終的には自分で決めさせてもらいますけどね」
lines.english: “Right. I’ll take that valuable opinion under advisement. Ultimately, though, I’ll be making the decision myself, whatever you may say.”

lines.japanese: と、まあ、日和子さんに罪悪感が残らないようフォローは入れつつも。
lines.english: So I made sure to add that, sparing Hiyoko any lingering guilt.

lines.japanese: しょーがない、マスターには悪いけど、明日にでもお断りの電話を入れておきましょう。
lines.english: It couldn’t be helped. I felt bad for the boss, but tomorrow I would call and decline.

lines.japanese: なあに、バイトなんて他にいくらでもありますよ、ええ。問題はむしろ、いかにテンションを落とさないで自分を保つかという、そっちの方だったりして。
lines.english: Hey, there are tons of other part-time jobs out there, sure. The real problem was keeping my energy from dropping so I could hold myself together.

lines.japanese: や、内緒ですけどね、本当は鷲介くんって、すっごくデリケートな男の子なんですよ。てへへ。
lines.english: The truth, just between us, is that Shusuke is a very sensitive boy. Tee hee.

lines.japanese: あー待て待て、落ちるな落ちるな。やばいやばい。こんなときは、えーと──
lines.english: Wait, wait. Don't sink. Don't sink. This was bad. Come on, what did we do at times like this—

lines.japanese: 世界が平和でありますように、だっけ？
lines.english: *May peace prevail on Earth*. Was that it?

lines.japanese: 「──あ、でもっ」
lines.english: “—Oh, but!”

lines.japanese: ほんじゃ、と去りかけたところで急遽付けたされた逆接の接続詞。
lines.english: I had nearly left with a casual 'well, then' when she hastily appended that adversative conjunction.

lines.japanese: 「はい？」
lines.english: “Yes?”

lines.japanese: 俺が向きなおったとき、日和子さんはわずか半歩だけ前に踏みだしていました。
lines.english: When I turned back, Hiyoko had taken the smallest half-step forward.

lines.japanese: 「でも、もし、さっきみたいに私が困ったとき、また庇ってくれるんだったら……」
lines.english: But if you'd stand up for me again whenever I get in trouble like before...

lines.japanese: 気が付けばいつの間にやら、あの日和子さんが──
lines.english: Before I knew it, that very Hiyoko had—

lines.japanese: 「賛、成……かも？」
lines.english: “Then I... might approve?”

lines.japanese: ──あのあったかい微笑みを浮かべておりました。
lines.english: —was wearing that warm smile of hers.

lines.japanese: それは完全に隙を突かれたと言いますか。
lines.english: You might say she had caught me entirely off guard.

lines.japanese: ぽろっ。
lines.english: Slip.
“—Whoa!”

lines.japanese: 指先からこぼれた若草色の乗車券を、俺は慌てて膝のあたりですくいあげました。
lines.english: I snatched the pale-green ticket out of the air at knee height.

lines.japanese: 落としてたまるかと。落ちてたまるかと。
lines.english: As if I would let it fall. As if I would let myself fall.

lines.japanese: なんてね。まさかね。そんなチェリーくさい中二男子じゃあるまいし？　羽田さん家のタカシくんじゃあるまいし？　たった笑顔ひとつで？　やられませんよ、ははん！
lines.english: Just kidding. As if. I wasn't some painfully virginal eighth grader. I wasn't little Takashi from the Haneda household. One smile, and I was supposed to be done for? Not a chance. Ha!

lines.japanese: 俺は深呼吸する代わりに、斜に構えて鼻をひとつ鳴らしました。
lines.english: Instead of taking a deep breath, I put on an air of cool detachment and snorted.

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ、まあ、それもご意見のひとつとして頂戴しつつ」
lines.english: “Well, then, I’ll accept that as one opinion among many.”

lines.japanese: 「あくまで決めるのは俺自身だがな！」
lines.english: “The decision, of course, remains mine and mine alone!”

lines.japanese: びしっと親指を立てる俺は流されない男。かっこいー。
lines.english: I thrust up a decisive thumb: a man who would never be swayed. So cool.

lines.japanese: 「あ、それと……もうひとつ、ありがとうございました」
lines.english: “Oh, and... thank you for one more thing.”

lines.japanese: 「は？　え、なにが……？」
lines.english: “Huh? For what...?”

lines.japanese: 「あのとき英里子さんに、私の本は面白いって言ってくれて……」
lines.english: “When you told Eriko that my book was interesting...”

lines.japanese: 「すぐに言えなかったけど……本当は、すごく嬉しかったんです」
lines.english: “I couldn’t say it right away, but... the truth is, it made me very happy.”

lines.japanese: 「そ、そーでしたか……」
lines.english: “I-is that so...”

lines.japanese: やばい。
lines.english: This was bad.

lines.japanese: やばい俺。このままこんな笑顔直視してたら、やばいかもしんない。
lines.english: Bad. Very bad. If I kept looking directly at that smile, I might be in real trouble.

lines.japanese: 「ま、まあ、そーゆーことで！」
lines.english: “W-well, anyway! That settles that!”

lines.japanese: 「あ、はい。おやすみなさい」
lines.english: “Oh. Yes. Good night.”

lines.japanese: 俺は逃げるように日和子さんと別れて、素早くホームへ向かいました。
lines.english: I fled from Hiyoko and hurried toward the platform.

lines.japanese: 「えええ、なんだろ俺」
lines.english: “What is wrong with me?”

lines.japanese: さっさと背中を向けて正解です。不覚にも血が上ってきて、顔が熱く感じられました。
lines.english: Good thing I'd turned around so fast. Before I knew it, blood had rushed to my face and it felt hot.

lines.japanese: しかし速やかに通りぬけようと思った改札機は、入出場兼用だったみたいです。切符を近づけた投入口が、到着したばかりの上り電車から降りてきたお客さんの列によって、反対側から塞がれてしまいました。
lines.english: Unfortunately, the ticket gate I meant to hurry through served both entrances and exits. Just as I brought my ticket toward the slot, the other side was blocked by a stream of passengers disembarking from a newly arrived inbound train.

lines.japanese: 「ああもうっ」
lines.english: “Oh, come on!”

lines.japanese: 仕方ないので、ひとつ右の改札機に回ろうとしたとき──
lines.english: I was about to move one gate to the right when—

lines.japanese: 「あれえ、いま帰りー？」
lines.english: “Ohhh, just heading home?”

lines.japanese: ──ひとつ左の改札機から出てきた、パンツスーツのお姉さんに声をかけられました。
lines.english: —a woman in a pantsuit emerged from the gate to my left and called out to me.

lines.japanese: 「おわっ、米田さん！？」
lines.english: “Whoa! Ms. Yoneda?!”

lines.japanese: び、びっくりした……。
lines.english: Th-that startled me...

lines.japanese: あ、ああ、そうか。そういえばこのひと、通勤にこの電車使ってるんだった。いや、でも日和子さんと別れたあとで良かった良かった。
lines.english: Ah, right. Of course. She took this train to work. Still, thank goodness I had already parted with Hiyoko.

lines.japanese: ……いや、べつに良かったとか悪かったとかの問題じゃないけど。
lines.english: ...Not that this was really about whether that was good or bad.

lines.japanese: 「ど、ども、お世話さまっす。やー、奇遇っすね」
lines.english: “H-hey, Ms. Yoneda. Fancy meeting you here.”

lines.japanese: 「へー、いままで遊んでたんだ。へー、私はいまから仕事」
lines.english: “Oh, so you’ve been out having fun till now. How nice. I’m on my way to work.”

lines.japanese: 「す、すいません」
lines.english: “S-sorry.”

lines.japanese: あまり嫌味な口調ではありませんでしたが、ぱりっとした戦闘衣装のオフィスレディを前に、ついつい弱気になってしまうフリーアルバイターでありました。
lines.english: Her tone was not particularly barbed, but faced with a proper career woman in a crisp suit of battle armor, this lowly free-floating part-timer could not help shrinking into himself.

lines.japanese: メンフリ編集部には米田さんよりもっとラフな格好をした編集さんが大勢いらっしゃいますが、彼女は自らに気合を入れるため、あえてスーツスタイルを好むのだそうです。いやはや、立派な心意気です。
lines.english: Plenty of editors at Men's Freeze dressed far more casually than Yoneda, but she apparently favored suits as a deliberate way of putting herself in a working frame of mind. An admirable attitude indeed.

lines.japanese: “だって私、こういう服に憧れてデスクワーク志望したんだもん”
lines.english: “I wanted a desk job because I always dreamed of wearing clothes like these.”

lines.japanese: ──なんて、制服の可愛さで志望校を選んじゃう、いまどきの受験生みたいなこともおっしゃってましたけどね。
lines.english: —Though she had also sounded rather like a modern-day student choosing a school because the uniform was cute.

lines.japanese: 「や、米田さんすごい！　めちゃめちゃ早朝出勤っすね！」
lines.english: “Wow, Ms. Yoneda! That's an incredibly early start!”

lines.japanese: 俺はコンコース中ほどに掛かった吊り時計を見上げながら手を叩きました。なにしろ日付が変わってまだほんの十分ぐらいです。
lines.english: I clapped as I looked up at the clock suspended over the middle of the concourse. After all, the date had changed barely ten minutes ago.

lines.japanese: 「ええー？　ここんとこずっとこんな感じだけどね……」
lines.english: “Really? It’s been like this every day lately...”

lines.japanese: 「家戻ったってさー、お風呂入って、三時間仮眠して、起きたら化粧してまた出勤。はあ……」
lines.english: “Even if I go home, all I do is take a bath, sleep for three hours, wake up, put on makeup, and head straight back to work. Sigh...”

lines.japanese: 「え、会社に仮眠室とかないんすか。それもう泊まりこんだ方が早いっすよ」
lines.english: “Doesn’t the office have a nap room or something? At that point, you’d save time by sleeping there.”

lines.japanese: 「だめだめ、お風呂だけは自分ちで入りたいの。狭いユニットだけどさ、せめてもの区切りっていうのかな。分かる、この気持ち？」
lines.english: No, no, I only wanna take baths at home. My bathroom's tiny and all-in-one, but... I dunno, it's like the bare minimum of keeping things separate. You get what I mean?

lines.japanese: 「……ま、分かんないよね」
lines.english: “...No, I suppose you wouldn’t.”

lines.japanese: 「エちょっ……なんすかその白い目！」
lines.english: “Wh—hey! What’s with that look?”

lines.japanese: 「もう、やめてくださいよそんな、ひとをニートみたいに。いちおう俺フリーアルバイターっすよ。いちおう経済大国ニッポンの一端をになう、社会の歯車っすよ。しかもときには潤滑油っすよ、鷲介ぬるぬるっすよ」
lines.english: “Come on, don't look at me like I'm some unemployed shut-in. I happen to be a working man—a small cog in the great economic power of Japan. Sometimes I'm even the lubricant. Slippery Shusuke, that's me.”

lines.japanese: 「それはさて置き、千歳君さっき電話くれたって？」
lines.english: “Setting that aside, I heard you called earlier?”

lines.japanese: 「さて置かれた社会の歯車！」
lines.english: “The cog in society has been set aside!”

lines.japanese: 「やー、ごめんねー。とにかく眠かったからさー、あんまり覚えてないんだよねー」
lines.english: “Sorry about that. I was so tired I barely remember any of it.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、電話口でオレオレ詐欺を撃退した夢だけは覚えてるけど」
lines.english: Oh, I do remember this dream where I scared off one of those 'It's me' phone scammers.

lines.japanese: 「いや、それたぶん夢じゃないっす。たぶん撃退されたの俺っす」
lines.english: “That probably wasn’t a dream. I’m pretty sure the person you drove off was me.”

lines.japanese: 「で、起きたあとケータイの履歴見たら、アレキサンダーの番号入ってるでしょ。またカケルかなーと思って、さっき彼んとこ、かけてみたんだー」
lines.english: “Anyway, when I woke up and checked my call history, Alexander’s number was there. I thought it might be Kakeru again, so I called him a little while ago.”

lines.japanese: 以前カケルくんがあの店から電話してきたことがあるのだと、米田さんは説明しました。
lines.english: Yoneda explained that Kakeru had once called her from the restaurant.

lines.japanese: 「そしたら『俺じゃなくてシュウちゃんでしょ』って」
lines.english: “And he said, ‘That wasn’t me. It must’ve been Shu.’”

lines.japanese: 「ええ、ええ、そうですそうです。シュウちゃんこと千歳ぬるぬる鷲介です」
lines.english: “Yes, yes, exactly. Shu, otherwise known as Slippery Shusuke Chitose.”

lines.japanese: 「ふふーん、聞いたよー？　君、多摩いづみと間違って、玉泉日和子とかいう子に声かけちゃったんだってぇ？」
lines.english: “Mm-hmm, I heard allll about it. You mistook some girl named Hiyoko Tamaizumi for Tama Izumi and went up to her, didn't you?”

lines.japanese: それがカケルくんの策略のせいだと分かっている、同情的な嘲笑。
lines.english: Sympathetic mockery. She knew it was Kakeru's scheme.

lines.japanese: 「あー、それねー……」
lines.english: “Ah. That...”

lines.japanese: 俺の方は、思いだして陰鬱な気分。
lines.english: That memory put me in a gloomy mood.

lines.japanese: 「ま、お耳に入ってんなら話は早いすけど」
lines.english: “Well, if you’ve already heard, that makes this easier.”

lines.japanese: 「あの、そーゆーわけなんで。来月の書籍紹介記事、俺にもう一枠いただけません？　や、もちろんノーギャラでいいっすから」
lines.english: “That’s the situation. So could I have one more slot in next month’s book column? I’ll do it for free, of course.”

lines.japanese: 「うーん……」
米田さんは半分ぐらい働く女性の顔になって、頭の中に御自分の担当ページを描いているようでした。
lines.english: Yoneda's expression went halfway professional as she mentally laid out the pages under her charge.

lines.japanese: 「そうねえ、キャパ的には空けられると思うけど……ま、いちお会社戻って確認してからね」
lines.english: “I think I can make room... but let me get back to the office and confirm first.”

lines.japanese: 「まじすか！　あざーっす！　ありがとうございます！」
lines.english: “Seriously?! 'Preciate it! Thank you so much!”

lines.japanese: 俺は自動改札機の前で深々と腰を折りました。いくつか積まれた問題が、これでひとつ解決しそうです。
lines.english: I bowed deeply in front of the ticket gate. Looked like one problem in the pile was about to get solved.

lines.japanese: 「おーし、ぬるっと行こー！」
lines.english: All right! Let's slide right through!

lines.japanese: 「ね。ところで玉泉日和子ってそれ、なに書いたひとなの？」
lines.english: Hey, by the way, what does Hiyoko Tamaizumi write?
“...What?”

lines.japanese: 自動改札機の前、ぬるっと行こうポーズのまま硬直する俺。
lines.english: I froze before the gates, still holding my smooth-and-slippery pose.

lines.japanese: 「私それ、さっきの電話で初めて聞いた名前なんだけど。なに、小説家？　詩人？　コラムニスト？」
lines.english: “That call was the first time I’d ever heard her name. What is she, a novelist? A poet? A columnist?”

lines.japanese: 「……た、ただちに調査いたします」
lines.english: “...I-I shall investigate immediately.”

lines.japanese: 硬直を解きつつ、目を逸らして回答。
lines.english: Breaking out of my pose, I looked away as I answered.

lines.japanese: そういえば俺は、いまだ玉泉先生のジャンルも作風も書名すらも知りませんでした。当たりまえだけど。
lines.english: Come to think of it, I still knew neither Tamaizumi's genre, nor her style, nor even the title of a single book. Naturally.

lines.japanese: でも成り行きとは言えそんな状態でファン名乗っちゃって、しかもあんなに喜ばせてるわけだから、とんでもない詐欺ですよね俺。日和子さんにバレないうち、早く本当のファンになっておかないと。
lines.english: Still, circumstances or not, I'd called myself a fan without even reading her book and made her that happy. I was a real scam artist. I needed to hurry up and become a genuine fan before Hiyoko found out.

lines.japanese: 「え……ちょっと、大丈夫なの？　千歳君の推薦ならって思ったんだけど、あんまり適当言ってるんだったらさすがに私だって困るよ？」
lines.english: “Um... are you sure this is okay? I only considered it because the recommendation came from you. If you’re just making things up, even I’m going to have a problem.”

lines.japanese: 「だ、大丈夫です！　俺を信じてください！」
lines.english: “I-it’s fine! Trust me!”

lines.japanese: 「信じろって言われても……じゃあ君は、読んだこともない本を信じてるの？」
lines.english: “You say that, but... do you trust a book you’ve never even read?”

lines.japanese: 「信じてます。信じまくります」
lines.english: I believe you. Totally, completely believe you.

lines.japanese: 「や、作者の方がとっても面白いひとなんです。だから、その作品もきっと面白いものに違いありません」
lines.english: “The author is a very interesting person. So I’m certain her work must be interesting too.”

lines.japanese: 「なにそのおめでたい理論。職業人として反論したい気もするけど、時間がもったいないからいまはいいや。君も彼女待たせてるみたいだし」
lines.english: “What kind of blissfully optimistic theory is that? As a professional, part of me wants to argue, but we don't have time. Besides, it looks like you're keeping your girlfriend waiting.”

lines.japanese: いきなり妙なことを口にする米田さん。
lines.english: Yoneda had suddenly said something very strange.

lines.japanese: 「は？　カノジョ？」
lines.english: “Huh? My girlfriend?”

lines.japanese: 「え、違うの？　だって、さっきからそこに立ってるけど……」
lines.english: “Oh, isn’t she? She’s been standing there this whole time...”

lines.japanese: 「だ、誰がですか？」
lines.english: “W-who has?”

lines.japanese: 「や、だから、いま君の後ろにいる──」
lines.english: “I mean the girl right behind you—”

lines.japanese: 米田さんがちょいっと突きあげた顎の先を追って、俺がおそるおそる振りむけば──
lines.english: Following the tilt of Yoneda's chin, I slowly, fearfully turned around—and—

lines.japanese: <10>\「ぎゃああああああああ──っ！」
lines.english: “AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAH!”

lines.japanese: <10>\　聞ーかーれーてーた──っ！！
lines.english: SHE—HEARD—EVERYTHIIIIING!
